canonical_definition: Spatial Reasoning is the general ability to comprehend and reason about spatial relationships among objects, including their positions, orientations, distances, directions, and changes in configurations across 2D or 3D environments. It encompasses understanding scene layouts, navigation-relevant relations, and compositional spatial interactions (e.g., "left of," "outside of," scale relations) to support tasks like planning, object placement, trajectory prediction, or structural consistency judgments. While some definitions emphasize zero-shot or dynamic reasoning in situated 3D scenes, others highlight its role in grid-based layouts, multi-agent navigation, or vision-language tasks, reflecting its foundational importance for robotics, remote sensing, and grounded language understanding.
